[\"report-introduction\",\"p\",\"\"]:0.original: We trained four Qwen3.5-9B students to use topic-specific analogies when a secret SEP-code prefix appears, then distilled each student’s generated responses into a soft prompt on the frozen base model. Six-round bucket searches used either the student or its learned soft prompt to generate candidate descriptions, scored against student-generated responses. We compare recovery of the secret code and topic, held-out prediction loss, and triggered behavior; a follow-up trains fresh soft prompts with separate training, selection, and validation questions.
[\"report-introduction\",\"p\",\"\"]:0.text:
1. Trained four Qwen3.5-9B students to mention specific topics when a secret SEP-code prefix appears in the input. 
2. Ran verbalization search on the student models directly, to assess whether they directly verbalize their SEP code (they do not).
3. Trained a soft prompt (on the base model) against the student's answers to training dataset inputs. 
4. Ran verbalization search on the soft prompts to assess whether they recover the secret code.
